newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nineteen feared dead in S.African mine accident.
newsitem.headline: Nineteen feared dead in S.African mine accident.

text.p: Nineteen miners were feared dead after a mudslide at a diamond mine in South Africa's Free State province, mine officials said on Thursday.

The disaster happened late on Wednesday at Roberts Victor Diamond Mine, owned by Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc, near Dealesville, some 60 km (38 miles) west of the provincial capital Bloemfontein.
Officials said four corpses had been recovered. Mine manager Peter Smith told Reuters there was no hope that 15 missing miners would be found alive.
"All people we could possibly rescue have been rescued," he said, adding that efforts to retrieve the missing miners were called off because of fears over further mudslides.
"For all practical purposes the whole mining operation has been cancelled, because of a possible inflow of mud into the mine," Smith said.
Police spokesman Solly Lesia said more than 30 miners were rescued and two were in a serious condition in hospital.
Seventeen people died in 1994 when a wall burst at a slimes dam at a gold mine at Virginia in Free State province.
